text:
Databases are essential tools for storing and organizing information. Most people first encounter *relational databases*, which use tables made of rows and columns. To interact with these, you use SQL (Structured Query Language) to write *queries*—for example, asking to find all customers over 30 years old. This structure is great for complex relationships, but it requires careful *data modeling*, meaning you must plan your tables before you start. 

However, not all data fits neatly into tables. *NoSQL databases*, like document stores, offer flexibility for rapidly changing or unstructured data. They are often faster for simple lookups. No matter which type you choose, using *indexes*—special structures that allow quick searching—is vital. Without them, queries can become painfully slow as your data grows. Understanding these fundamentals helps you choose the right tool for your project.
